BURHAN:v3p143/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p143/r3.speaker: الكسائي
BURHAN:v3p143/r3.claim: Al-Kisa’i allows an unexpressed agent whenever context identifies it: the soul reaches the collarbones, the sun disappears, punishment descends, or a messenger comes to Solomon.
BURHAN:v3p143/r3.anchor: وجوز الكسائي حذفه مطلقا إذا ما وجد ما يدل عليه

BURHAN:v3p143/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p143/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p143/r4.claim: The author’s correction is that the agent in these examples is implicit, not deleted; he distinguishes the two grammatical analyses.
BURHAN:v3p143/r4.anchor: والحق أنه في المذكورات مضمر لا محذوف وقد سبق الفرق بينهما

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p482/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p482/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p482/r5.claim: The singular verb ja’a grammatically agrees with the delegation, indicating a whole group came to Solomon.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p482/r5.anchor: The singular tense of the verb

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p483/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p483/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p483/r1.claim: Both the queen’s and Solomon’s wording indicates a whole delegation came; Solomon rejected its gifts and said God had already granted him greater blessings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p483/r1.anchor: a whole delegation came to meet him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p483/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p483/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p483/r2.claim: Solomon’s concise reference to God’s gifts includes wealth, status, wisdom, and his empire.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p483/r2.anchor: encompass wealth, status, and wisdom as well as the empire Solomon (sws) had.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p483/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p483/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p483/r3.claim: Solomon’s reply demands submission and God’s rule, not friendship bought with gifts; accepting would mean allowing disbelief and polytheism to rule God’s earth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p483/r3.anchor: his purpose was to make God’s directives prevail in the land

STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.claim: The account of Solomon's miraculous host and encounter with the Queen of Sheba ends with her embracing faith in the One God.
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.anchor: Solomon with his miraculous host of men, jinn, and birds and his encounter with the Queen of Sheba, who eventually comes before Solomon

TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r6.claim: In the account of the gift's arrival, the pronoun for what came may refer either to the wealth itself or to the messenger who brought it.
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r6.anchor: ضمير جاء للمال الذي أهدي إليه أو للرسول الذي جاء بالهدية

TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r7.claim: Solomon's question about supplying him with wealth is a rebuke to the envoy and sender, using a present addressee for the absent party as the queen earlier did; addressing only the envoys is wrong because they did not send the gift.
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r7.anchor: والاستفهام في قوله { أتمدونن بمال } للتوبيخ والخطاب للرسول والمرسل بتغليب الحاضر على الغائب

TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r8.claim: The indefinite word wealth belittles the gift against God's grants of kingdom and prophethood; Solomon further reproaches their pride and delight in a gift they value so highly.
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r8.anchor: وتنكير المال للتحقير، والمراد بما آتاني الله الملك والنبوة

TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r9.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r9.claim: Another reading takes their joy in the gift as joy in gifts received, reflecting their love of accumulating wealth, while Solomon says he disregards worldly property.
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r9.anchor: وقيل المراد بهديتكم الهدية التي تهدي إليكم، والمعنى بل أنتم تفرحون بما يهدى إليكم

TABATABAI:27:15-44#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:15-44#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:15-44#4/r1.claim: Because the gift showed refusal of Solomon’s demand for submission, he judged them unbelieving and threatened a superior army; its dispatch and their humiliation depended on their refusal.
TABATABAI:27:15-44#4/r1.anchor: قدر بحسب المقام أنهم غير مسلمين له فهددهم بإرسال جنود لا قبل لهم بها

TABATABAI:27:15-44#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:15-44#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:15-44#4/r2.claim: Although the wording attaches the army’s arrival to the messenger’s return without an explicit condition, the intended meaning remains conditional on their not submitting.
TABATABAI:27:15-44#4/r2.anchor: فرع إتيانهم بالجنود على رجوع الرسول من غير أن يشترطه بعدم إتيانهم مسلمين

TABATABAI:27:15-44#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:15-44#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:15-44#4/r3.claim: The narrative context indicates that Solomon returned the gift and refused to accept it.
TABATABAI:27:15-44#4/r3.anchor: والسياق يشهد أنه عليه السلام رد إليهم هديتهم ولم يقبلها منهم.

THALABI:v7p207/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p207/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p207/r3.claim: Solomon ordered the jinn to pave a nine-farsakh field with gold and silver bricks and build gold-and-silver walls around it.
THALABI:v7p207/r3.anchor: ثم أمرهم أن يبسطوا من موضعه الذي هو فيه إلى تسع فراسخ ميدانا واحدا بلبنات الذهب والفضة

THALABI:v7p207/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p207/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p207/r4.claim: Solomon had unusual sea creatures brought, then ordered them lined along both sides of the field and fed.
THALABI:v7p207/r4.anchor: يا نبي الله إنا رأينا دواب في بحر كذا وكذا منمرة منقطعة مختلفة ألوانها، لها أجنحة وأعراف ونواصي

THALABI:v7p207/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p207/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p207/r5.claim: Solomon assembled jinn children, sat amid eighty thousand chairs, and arrayed jinn, humans, demons, beasts, predators, vermin, and birds for farsakhs on either side.
THALABI:v7p207/r5.anchor: ووضع له أربعون ألف كرسي عن يمينه ومثلها عن يساره، وأمر الشياطين أن يصطفوا صفوفا فراسخ

THALABI:v7p207/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p207/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p207/r6.claim: Seeing Solomon's extraordinary court and animals defecating on the gold and silver paving, the envoys felt small and ashamed of their gifts.
THALABI:v7p207/r6.anchor: فلما رأى القوم الميدان ونظروا إلى ملك سليمان (عليه السلام) ورأوا الدواب التي لم تر أعينهم مثلها تروث على لبنات الذهب والفضة

THALABI:v7p207/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p207/r7.speaker: بعض الروايات
THALABI:v7p207/r7.claim: One account says Solomon left a gap in the paved road matching the envoys' bricks; fearing suspicion when they saw it, they placed their bricks there.
THALABI:v7p207/r7.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات أن سليمان (عليه السلام) لما أمر بفرش الميدان بلبنات الذهب والفضة أمرهم أن يتركوا على طريقهم موضعا

THALABI:v7p208/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p208/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p208/r1.claim: The envoys passed safely through ranks of jinn, humans, birds, predators, and beasts; Solomon welcomed them warmly, asked their news, and received the queen's letter from their chief.
THALABI:v7p208/r1.anchor: فكانوا يمرون على كردوس كردوس من الجن والإنس والطير والسباع والوحش حتى وقفوا بين يدي سليمان

THALABI:v7p208/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p208/r2.speaker: جبريل عليه السلام
THALABI:v7p208/r2.claim: Gabriel told Solomon the closed box held an unpierced pearl and a carnelian bead pierced through a crooked hole; the envoy confirmed this and asked him to pierce and thread them.
THALABI:v7p208/r2.anchor: وجاءه جبرئيل (عليه السلام) فأخبره بما في الحقة فقال: إن فيها درة يتيمة غير مثقوبة وجزعة مثقوبة معوجة الثقب

THALABI:v7p208/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p208/r3.speaker: الأرضة
THALABI:v7p208/r3.claim: When humans, jinn, and demons could not pierce the pearl, a termite carried a hair through it; asked her wish, she requested her sustenance in a tree, which Solomon granted.
THALABI:v7p208/r3.anchor: ترسل الى الأرضة فجاءت الأرضة وأخذت شعرة في فيها فدخلت فيها حتى خرجت

THALABI:v7p208/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p208/r4.speaker: دودة بيضاء
THALABI:v7p208/r4.claim: A white worm threaded the bent hole in the bead; when asked what she wished for, she requested fruit as her sustenance, and Solomon granted it.
THALABI:v7p208/r4.anchor: فقالت دودة بيضاء: أنا لها يا رسول الله، فأخذت الدودة الخيط في فيها ودخلت الثقب

THALABI:v7p208/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p208/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p208/r5.claim: Solomon distinguished the girls from the boys by how each took water, washed the face, and poured it over the inner or outer forearm.
THALABI:v7p208/r5.anchor: أمرهم أن يغسلوا وجوههم وأيديهم فكانت الجارية تأخذ الماء من الآنية بإحدى يديها

THALABI:v7p208/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p208/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p208/r6.claim: After identifying the attendants, Solomon returned the gift.
THALABI:v7p208/r6.anchor: فميز بينهن بذلك ثم رد سليمان (عليه السلام) الهدية.

THALABI:v7p208/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p208/r7.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب وابن عامر وعاصم والكسائي وخلف والباقون
THALABI:v7p208/r7.claim: The readers differ on أتمدونن: Hamza and Yaqub use one doubled nun; Ibn Amir, Asim, al-Kisai, and Khalaf use two light nuns without the yāʾ, while the rest retain it.
THALABI:v7p208/r7.anchor: فقرأ حمزة ويعقوب أتمدوني بنون واحدة مشددة، غيرهما بنونين خفيفتين وحذف الياء، ابن عامر وعاصم والكسائي وخلف

THALABI:v7p209/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p209/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p209/r1.claim: Solomon says what God gave him is better than the gift, explaining that its givers prize worldly display and that God already granted him wealth, religion, prophethood, and wisdom.
THALABI:v7p209/r1.anchor: فما آتاني الله خير مما آتاكم بل أنتم بهديتكم تفرحون لأنكم أهل مفاخرة الدنيا والمكابرة بها

RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r5.claim: Solomon’s question shows how little he cared about the offered wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r5.anchor: فأظهر بهذا الكلام قلة الاكتراث بذلك المال

RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r6.claim: One reading takes hadiyya as the gift itself, a noun that may be attributed to giver or recipient; here it is attributed to its recipients.
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r6.anchor: الهدية اسم للمهدي ، كما أن العطية اسم للمعطي

RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r7.claim: On that reading, God gave Solomon the supreme happiness of religion and abundant worldly goods, so a gift could not tempt him; the queen’s people rejoice in gifts, unlike him.
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r7.anchor: آتاني الدين الذي هو السعادة القصوى

RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r8.claim: A second view says they rejoice because they were able to give a gift like this one.
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r8.anchor: بل أنتم بهديتكم هذه التي أهديتموها تفرحون من حيث إنكم قدرتم على إهداء مثلها

RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r9.claim: A third view takes Solomon to mean that they should take their gift back and rejoice in it.
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r9.anchor: بل أنتم من حقكم أن تأخذوا هديتكم

BURSEVI:v6p252/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252/r1.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p252/r1.claim: Al-Kashifi says Solomon ordered water so the boys and girls could wash; girls transferred water between hands before splashing, while boys took it from the vessel and splashed directly.
BURSEVI:v6p252/r1.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (سليمان آب طلبيد غلمان وجواري را فرمودكه از غبارراه روى بشوييد)

BURSEVI:v6p252/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p252/r2.claim: Solomon addressed both the envoy and the queen, using masculine plural for the present person over the absent one.
BURSEVI:v6p252/r2.anchor: للرسول والمرسل تغليبا للحاضر على الغائب أي قال بعد ما جرى بينه وبينهم من قصة الحقة وغيرها

BURSEVI:v6p252/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p252/r3.claim: The speech came after the episode of the case and other tests, not immediately on arrival as the surface wording might suggest.
BURSEVI:v6p252/r3.anchor: أي قال بعد ما جرى بينه وبينهم من قصة الحقة وغيرها لا أنه خاطبهم به أول ما جاؤوه

BURSEVI:v6p252/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p252/r4.claim: Atamuddūnani is originally atamuddūnani with a final yāʾ, omitted because the kasra indicates it; the interrogative hamza expresses rejection.
BURSEVI:v6p252/r4.anchor: أصله أتمودنني فحذفت الياء اكتفاء بالكسرة الدالة عليها والهمزة الاستفهامية للإنكار.

BURSEVI:v6p252/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p252/r5.claim: Imdād means supplying or assisting and takes its second object with bi; Solomon asks whether they offer him an increase through wealth.
BURSEVI:v6p252/r5.anchor: والإمداد (مدد كردن) ويعدى إلى المفعول الثاني بالباء

BURSEVI:v6p252/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p252/r6.claim: Solomon treats their wealth as paltry; māl is linked to its continual passing or being acquired, and is also called ʿaraḍ.
BURSEVI:v6p252/r6.anchor: {بمال} حقير وسمي مالا لكونه مائلا أبدا ونائلا ولذلك يسمى عرضا

BURSEVI:v6p252/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252/r7.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v6p252/r7.claim: Al-Mufradāt cites the saying that wealth is a prostitute, one day in the perfumer’s house and another in the veterinarian’s.
BURSEVI:v6p252/r7.anchor: وعلى هذا دل من قال : المال قحبة يكون يوما في بيت عطار ويوما يكون في بيت بيطار كما في "المفردات" :

BURSEVI:v6p252/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p252/r8.claim: Mā in the clause is a relative pronoun: what God has given is better than their riches.
BURSEVI:v6p252/r8.anchor: ثم علل هذا الإنكار بقوله : {فمآ} موصولة {الله خير} مما رأيتم آثاره من النبوة والملك

BURSEVI:v6p252/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p252/r9.claim: God’s gift of prophethood and a kingdom beyond worldly comparison is better than their wealth, leaving no need or value for their gift.
BURSEVI:v6p252/r9.anchor: {خير ممآ ءاتااكم} من المال ومتاع الدنيا فلاحاجة إلى هديتكم ولا وقع لها عندي.

BURSEVI:v6p252/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p252/r10.claim: A Persian couplet says the world is carrion in the eyes of one oriented toward the higher realm.
BURSEVI:v6p252/r10.anchor: آنكه رواز كندجانب علوي وهماي دنيي اندر نطر همت أو مردارست

BURSEVI:v6p252/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252/r11.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v6p252/r11.claim: The Mathnawī contrasts spiritual proof and kingdoms beyond water and clay with worldly sovereignty, mere bondage mistaken for a throne.
BURSEVI:v6p252/r11.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" : من سليمان من نخواهم ملكتان بلكه من برهان ازهر هلكتان

BURSEVI:v6p252/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252/r12.speaker: جعفر الصادق
BURSEVI:v6p252/r12.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says worldly life is too insignificant before God, prophets, and friends to rejoice or grieve over; scholars and wise people should not rejoice in its goods.
BURSEVI:v6p252/r12.anchor: قال جعفر الصادق : الدنيا أصغر قدرا عند الله وعند أنبيائه وأوليائه من أن يفرحوا بشيء منها أو يحزنوا

BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r1.claim: The phrase concerns gift recipients; here it means people rejoice at gifts made to them because they love added wealth and know only outward life.
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r1.anchor: {بل أنتم بهديتكم تفرحون} المضاف إليه المهدى إليه.

BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r2.claim: The author prefers the contextual reading that worldly people rejoice when gifts come to them, which best fits the preceding story.
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r2.anchor: والمعنى بل أنتم بما يهدى إليكم تفرحون حبا لزيادة المال لما إنكم لا تعلمون إلا ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا

BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r3.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r3.claim: Al-Irshād instead takes this as rebuke for rejoicing in their own gift through pride, indebtedness, and self-importance, as the pearl test and disguises suggest.
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r3.anchor: وفي "الإرشاد" : إضراب عما ذكر من إنكار الإمداد بالمال إلى التوبيخ بفرحهم بهديتهم التي أهدوها إليه افتخارا

BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r4.claim: Bursevī rejects that reading: the envoys saw Solomon’s vast kingdom, deemed their own goods insignificant, and nearly cast aside the bricks; the case and pearl questions were tests, not gifts.
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r4.anchor: يقول الفقير : فيه إنهم لما رأوا ما أنعم الله به على سليمان من الملك الكبير استقلوا بما عندهم حتى هموا بطرح اللبنات

BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r5.speaker: التأويلات
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r5.claim: The inward lesson is to choose religious commands and lasting faith over abundant worldly benefit: Solomon valued religion, nearness, and afterlife ranks above mortal ornaments, while worldly people rejoice in them through ignorance of lasting felicity.
BURSEVI:v6p252#2/r5.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : يشير إلى أن الهدية موجبة لاستمالة القلوب ولكن أهل الدين لما عارضهم أمر ديني في مقابلة منافع كثيرة دنيوية

STUDYQURAN:27:36/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:36/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:36/r1.claim: The Queen of Sheba’s wealth could not rival Solomon’s; as a prophet, he was not motivated to acquire worldly possessions for their own sake.
STUDYQURAN:27:36/r1.anchor: worldly possessions were no match for those of Solomon (Ṭ), who in any case was a prophet

STUDYQURAN:27:36/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:36/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:36/r2.claim: Their exulting in the gift means they celebrate their wealth and power rather than expressing generosity or goodness.
STUDYQURAN:27:36/r2.anchor: celebrating their own wealth and power rather than a manifestation of generosity or goodness (Ṭ).

TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r4.claim: Arabic may report a matter involving one person in the plural when it is not focusing on a particular, individually identified person; that explains the plural envoys followed by singular Solomon.
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r4.anchor: هذا نظير ما قد بينا قبل من إظهار العرب الخبر في أمر كان من واحد على وجه الخبر عن جماعة إذا لم يقصد

TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r5.speaker: قيل
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r5.claim: Another explanation is that the queen sent one envoy, so the singular means when the messenger came to Solomon; the singular command return to them is cited as evidence.
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r5.anchor: وقد قيل: إن الرسول الذي وجهته ملكة سبأ إلى سليمان كان امرءا واحدا

TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r6.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh has the plural jāʾū, matching the plural envoys in wording, while the canonical singular matches the underlying sense.
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r6.anchor: وقد ذكر أن ذلك في قراءة عبد الله (فلما جاءوا سليمان) على الجمع، وذلك للفظ قوله: {بم يرجع المرسلون}

TAB-FULL:v18p58/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p58/r1.speaker: بعض قراء البصرة
TAB-FULL:v18p58/r1.claim: Some Basran readers use two nūns and retain the yāʾ in connected recitation but omit it at pause.
TAB-FULL:v18p58/r1.anchor: قرأه بعض قراء البصرة بنونين، وإثبات الياء في الوصل وحذفها في الوقف

TAB-FULL:v18p58/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p58/r2.speaker: بعض قراء الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v18p58/r2.claim: Some Kufan readers geminate the nūn and retain the yāʾ.
TAB-FULL:v18p58/r2.anchor: وقرأه بعض قراء الكوفة بتشديد النون وإثبات الياء

TAB-FULL:v18p58/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p58/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p58/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī accepts all these readings as sound, close in meaning, and well-known in Arabic speech.
TAB-FULL:v18p58/r3.anchor: وكل هذه القراءات متقاربات وجميعها صواب، لأنها معروفة في لغات العرب، مشهورة في منطقها.

TAB-FULL:v18p58#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p58#2/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v18p58#2/r2.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says the gifts included male and female attendants, fine-bred horses, and other worldly goods; Solomon had no need for them and sent them back with the threat of an army they could not resist.
TAB-FULL:v18p58#2/r2.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه، قال: " لما أتت الهدايا سليمان فيها الوصائف والوصفاء، والخيل العراب، وأصناف من أصناف الدنيا

TABRISI:27:32-35/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:32-35/r1.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب
TABRISI:27:32-35/r1.claim: Hamza and Yaqub read أتمدوني with one assimilated, geminated nūn.
TABRISI:27:32-35/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة ويعقوب أتمدوني بنون واحدة مشددة على الإدغام

TABRISI:27:32-35/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:32-35/r2.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:27:32-35/r2.claim: The remaining readers pronounce two distinct nūns.

TABRISI:27:36-37/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:36-37/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:36-37/r2.claim: Suleiman rejects their attempt to add wealth to his resources: the question is a denial, since he has no need of their money.
TABRISI:27:36-37/r2.anchor: أي تزيدونني مالا وهذا استفهام إنكار يعني أنه لا يحتاج إلى مالهم

TABRISI:27:36-37/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:36-37/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:36-37/r3.claim: What God gave Suleiman—kingdom, prophethood, and wisdom—is better than their worldly possessions.
TABRISI:27:36-37/r3.anchor: أي ما أعطاني الله من الملك والنبوة والحكمة خير مما أعطاكم من الدنيا وأموالهم

TABRISI:27:36-37/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:36-37/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:36-37/r4.claim: They rejoice in gifts among themselves, but Suleiman does not; this signals his indifference to worldly wealth.
TABRISI:27:36-37/r4.anchor: إذا هدى بعضكم إلى بعض وأما أنا فلا أفرح بها أشار إلى قلة اكتراثه بأموال الدنيا.

TABRISI:27:36-37/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:36-37/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:36-37/r7.claim: After Suleiman rejects the gift and distinguishes the attendants, the envoys realize he is a prophet rather than a king tempted by money.
TABRISI:27:36-37/r7.anchor: فلما رد سليمان الهدية وميز بين الغلمان والجواري إلى غير ذلك علموا أنه نبي مرسل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r1.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r1.claim: Al-Farra’ and al-Zajjaj say the one who came to Solomon was the envoy; al-Zajjaj also allows that the gift itself arrived, while “return to them” addresses the envoy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r1.anchor: أي: جاء الرسول سليمان؛ قاله الفراء والزجاج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r2.speaker: نافع من رواية المسيبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r2.claim: Al-Musayyibi reports Nafiʿ reading with one ungeminated nūn and a ya, omitting the second nūn attached to the first-person pronoun; dropping the first would be erroneous.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r2.anchor: عن نافع: {أتمدون} خفيفة النون بنون واحدة، وياء على حذف النون الثانية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r3.speaker: حمزة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r3.claim: Hamza reads with one doubled nūn, assimilating the first nūn into the second.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة: {أتمدوني} بنون واحدة مشددة أدغم الأولى في الثانية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r4.speaker: القراء بنونين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r4.claim: Readers who pronounce both nūns without assimilation do so because the second nūn is optional, as shown by ordinary speech that omits it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r4.anchor: ومن قرأ بنونين وجمع بين المثلين ولم يدغم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r5.claim: Solomon rejects their offering money, asking why they would supply him with wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r5.anchor: ومعنى قوله: {أتمدونن بمال} إنكار عليهم إهداءهم إليه، وما أتوه به من المال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r6.claim: What God gave Solomon—Islam, prophethood, and kingship—is better than what the people gave him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r6.anchor: أي: ما أعطانى من الإسلام والنبوة والملك خير مما أعطاكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r7.claim: Muqatil says people rejoice when exchanging gifts, but Solomon does not rejoice in them and wants them to accept Islam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p230/r7.anchor: يعني: إذا أهدى بعضكم إلى بعض، وأما أنا فلا أفرح بها إنما أريد منكم الإسلام. قاله مقاتل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r3.claim: Solomon rejects the offer because God gave him religion, prophethood, and wisdom, better than their worldly goods.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r3.anchor: فما آتاني الله } من الدين والنبوة والحكمة { خير مما آتاكم } من الدنيا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r4.claim: They rejoice in gifts because they compete for worldly abundance.

QASHANI:27:35-36/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:35-36/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:35-36/r3.claim: What God has given Solomon is certain knowledge, sacred realities, intellectual pleasures, and luminous visions, better than sensory, imaginary, and illusory adornments.
QASHANI:27:35-36/r3.anchor: من المعارف اليقينية والحقائق القدسية واللذات العقلية والمشاهدات النورية

QASHANI:27:35-36/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:35-36/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:35-36/r4.claim: The queen's party rejoices in its gift; Solomon's party rejoices in what comes from God, not in the things the gift represents.
QASHANI:27:35-36/r4.anchor: وإنما فرحنا بما هو من عند الله لا بما ذكر

ELMALILI:27:32-39#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:32-39#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:32-39#2/r8.claim: When the envoy reaches Solomon, Solomon refuses the gift.
ELMALILI:27:32-39#2/r8.anchor: vaktâ ki gönderilen, Süleyman’a vardı hediyeyi kabul etmeyip şu suretle reddetti.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:36/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:36/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:36/r1.claim: A prophet’s mission is to convey God’s religion and open a way out of deviant beliefs, not wage war for booty or extort gifts; Solomon rejects the queen’s gifts but threatens an army if they will not submit.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:36/r1.anchor: Peygamberin görevi insanlarla savaşarak ganimet elde etmek veya savaş tehdidiyle hediye almak değil, Allah’ın dinini tebliğ etmek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:36/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:36/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:36/r3.claim: The story implies that a female ruler acted with greater prudence than male statesmen.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:36/r3.anchor: Bu kıssada bir kadın yöneticinin erkek devlet adamlarından daha basiretli davrandığının ima edilmesi de ilgi çekicidir

BURHAN:v1p398/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p398/r2.speaker: أبو العباس
BURHAN:v1p398/r2.claim: The omitted yāʾ in فما آتاني marks Solomon’s knowledge and prophethood as an enduring, otherworldly gift that is better than the perishable worldly gifts given to the envoys.
BURHAN:v1p398/r2.anchor: حذفت الياء لاعتبار ما آتاه الله من العلم والنبوة

SULAMI:v2p90/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p90/r1.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p90/r1.claim: Jaʿfar says the world is too small in God’s sight, and to prophets and saints, for them to rejoice over it or grieve for it.
SULAMI:v2p90/r1.anchor: قال جعفر : الدنيا اصغر عند الله وعند انبيائه وأوليائه من أن يفرحوا بها ويحزنوا عليها

ITQAN:v3p138/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p138/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p138/r1.claim: A definite subject with an affirmative predicate can restrict the predicate; here, after Solomon rejects the offer, بل means that they alone rejoice in their gift, denying that he rejoices in it.
ITQAN:v3p138/r1.anchor: فإن المقصود نفي فرحه هو بالهدية لا إثبات الفرح لهم بهديتهم

ITQAN:v3p138/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p138/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p138/r4.claim: An indefinite subject with an affirmative predicate restricts by kind (a man, not a woman) or number (one man, not two).
ITQAN:v3p138/r4.anchor: نحو ( رجل جاءني ) فيفيد التخصيص إما بالجنس

ITQAN:v3p138/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p138/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p138/r6.claim: Al-Suyuti presents the preceding constructions as the substance of ʿAbd al-Qahir's view, followed by al-Sakkaki with added conditions and detail.
ITQAN:v3p138/r6.anchor: هذا حاصل رأي الشيخ عبد القاهر ووافقه السكاكي وزاد شروطا وتفاصيل

ITQAN:v3p138/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p138/r7.speaker: الشيخ بهاء الدين
ITQAN:v3p138/r7.claim: Emphasis without restriction is distinguished from restrictive emphasis only by the demands of context and discourse.
ITQAN:v3p138/r7.anchor: قال الشيخ بهاء الدين ولا يتميز ذلك إلا بما يقتضيه الحال وسياق الكلام

ITQAN:v3p138/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p138/r8.speaker: ابن الأثير وابن النفيس
ITQAN:v3p138/r8.claim: Ibn al-Athir, Ibn al-Nafis, and others say that placing the predicate before the subject conveys exclusivity.
ITQAN:v3p138/r8.anchor: ذكر ابن الأثير وابن النفيس وغيرهما أن تقديم الخبر على المبتدأ يفيد الاختصاص

ITQAN:v3p138/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p138/r9.speaker: صاحب الفلك الدائر
ITQAN:v3p138/r9.claim: The author reports that the author of al-Falak al-Daʾir rejects this rule, claiming no one held it.
ITQAN:v3p138/r9.anchor: ورده صاحب الفلك الدائر بأنه لم يقل به أحد

ITQAN:v3p138/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p138/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p138/r10.claim: Al-Suyuti rejects that objection: al-Sakkaki and others explicitly say fronting an element normally delayed gives restriction, as in “Tamimi am I.”
ITQAN:v3p138/r10.anchor: وهو ممنوع فقد صرح السكاكي وغيره بأن تقديم ما رتبته التأخير يفيده

ITQAN:v3p138/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p138/r11.speaker: السكاكي
ITQAN:v3p138/r11.claim: Al-Sakkaki says that explicitly mentioning the subject can convey restriction.
ITQAN:v3p138/r11.anchor: ذكر السكاكي أنه قد ذكر ليفيد التخصيص

ITQAN:v3p138/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p138/r12.speaker: صاحب الإيضاح
ITQAN:v3p138/r12.claim: The author of al-Idah objects to al-Sakkaki's claim that mentioning the subject conveys restriction.

ITQAN:v4p389/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p389/r20.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p389/r20.claim: The person who came to Solomon was named Mundhir.
ITQAN:v4p389/r20.anchor: ﴿ فلما جاء سليمان ﴾ إسم الجائي منذر

ITQAN:v2p395/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p395/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام
ITQAN:v2p395/r1.claim: Abu Ubayd reconciles the disagreement: some Qur'anic words had foreign origins, but Arabs naturalized them into Arabic before revelation, so both the Arabic and foreign-origin claims are true.
ITQAN:v2p395/r1.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام بعد أن حكى القول بالوقوع عن الفقهاء والمنع عن العربية

ITQAN:v2p395/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p395/r2.speaker: الجواليقي وابن الجوزي
ITQAN:v2p395/r2.claim: Al-Jawaliqi, Ibn al-Jawzi, and others favor Abu Ubayd's reconciliation of Arabic usage with foreign etymology.
ITQAN:v2p395/r2.anchor: ومال إلى هذا القول الجواليقي وابن الجوزي وآخرون

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r1.claim: The passage lists examples of verbal pairing and tajnīs, including غبي/أريب, هوى هوى, باب بابل, and the contrast between الأعلى and الأسفل.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r1.anchor: يعشى عن المجد الغبي ولن ترى في سؤدد أربا لغير اريب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r2.claim: Good sajʿ appears in prayers, prose, and old sayings when cadence does not force wording away from its meaning; the cited examples remain apt and natural.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r2.anchor: فلا مجد إلا بفعال ولا فعال إلا بمال وقول ابن العميد فإن الابقاء على خدم السلطان عدل الابقاء على ماله

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r3.speaker: النبي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r3.claim: The Prophet’s sayings about injustice as darkness, charity, and entering Paradise exemplify cadence whose phrasing is not chosen at the expense of meaning.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r3.anchor: وذلك كقول النبي الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامه وقوله لا تزال أمتي بخير ما لم تر الغنى مغنما

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r4.claim: A Bedouin complained to a governor in rhyming phrases about his mounts, clothes, and companions; the governor criticized his sajʿ, but the author says the wording suited the complaint rather than being forced.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r4.anchor: إنكار العامل السجع حتى قال فكيف أقول وذاك انه لم يعلم أصلح لما أراد من هذه الألفاظ

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r5.speaker: الجاحظ
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r5.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ explains that ركاب specifically expresses the complainant’s meaning; replacing it with camels, she-camels, or other terms would miss that nuance.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p8/r5.anchor: وقال الجاحظ لانه لو قال حلات إبلى أو جمالى أو نوقى أو بعرانى أو صرمتي

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p373/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p373/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p373/r1.claim: In ordinary usage, shara is an exchange of property for property: the buyer provides the price and the seller the goods.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p373/r1.anchor: الشرى في العرف : اعتياض مال بمال فالمشتري : باذل الثمن والبائع : باذل المثمن .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p373/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p373/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p373/r2.claim: شرى can mean either buying or selling, making it a word with opposite meanings; the cited verse uses it for selling.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p373/r2.anchor: يقال : شرى الرجل الشيء بمعنى : اشتراه وشراه أيضا بمعنى : باعه ، فهي كلمة من الأضداد .

FARRA:v2p292/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p292/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p292/r10.claim: Although the envoy was reportedly one woman, the queen uses the plural for him; the next verse's singular means “when the messenger came to Solomon.”
FARRA:v2p292/r10.anchor: رسولها- فيما ذكروا- امرأة واحدة فجمعت وإنما هو رسول

FARRA:v2p292/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p292/r11.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v2p292/r11.claim: Abd Allah reads the plural “when they came to Solomon,” matching the earlier plural “messengers”; singular and plural are both valid for the single envoy.
FARRA:v2p292/r11.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله (فلما جاءوا سليمان) لما قال (المرسلون)

FARRA:v2p293/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p293/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p293/r4.claim: Abd Allah and Hamza read two nūns with yāʾ; Hamza assimilates them with a doubled nūn. ʿĀṣim reads two nūns without yāʾ; all forms are sound.
FARRA:v2p293/r4.anchor: عبد الله بنونين وباء مثبتة. وقرأها حمزة

FARRA:v2p293/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p293/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p293/r5.claim: The yāʾ is absent from the written text in ā-tāni; readers who permit adding omitted yāʾs and wāws can restore it, but al-Farrāʾ prefers the consonantal text when Arab usage and the readers support it.
FARRA:v2p293/r5.anchor: اتباع المصحف إذا وجدت له وجها من كلام العرب وقراءة القراء أحب إلي من خلافه

FARRA:v2p293/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p293/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p293/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ does not recommend Abu ʿAmr's additions, including a yāʾ in inna hādhayni and a wāw in fa-aṣṣaddaq; he will not venture the former reading.
FARRA:v2p293/r6.anchor: لساحران) ولست أجترئ على ذلك وقرأ (فأصدق وأكون)

NAHHAS:v3p210/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p210/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p210/r5.claim: Assimilating the first nun into the second is allowed even though it creates two adjacent vowelless consonants.
NAHHAS:v3p210/r5.anchor: وإن شئت أدغمت النون في النون فذلك جائز وإن كان فيه جمع بين ساكنين

SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r1.claim: The messenger is omitted after “when he came to Solomon,” implied by the Queen’s statement that she would send; it means the class of messengers, not one individual.
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r1.anchor: أضمره لدلالة قولها " مرسلة " فإنه يستلزم رسولا. والمراد به الجنس

SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r2.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads jāʾū and later fa-irjiʿū, matching the plural messengers addressed by Solomon.
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r2.anchor: ولذلك قرأ عبد الله " فلما جاؤوا " وقرأ " فارجعوا " إليهم

SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r3.claim: Atumiddūnan is an interrogative of rejection.
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r3.anchor: استفهام إنكار. وقرأ حمزة بإدغام نون الرفع في نون الوقاية

SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r4.speaker: حمزة
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r4.claim: Ḥamza assimilates the indicative nūn into the nūn of protection; the yāʾ is omitted in pause and retained in continuation.
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بإدغام نون الرفع في نون الوقاية

SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r5.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r5.claim: The remaining readers retain two nūns; the yāʾ patterns vary: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr with Ḥamza, Ibn Kathīr in both positions, and the rest omit it in both.
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r5.anchor: والباقون بنونين على الأصل. وأما الياء فإن نافعا وأبا عمرو كحمزة

SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r6.speaker: نافع
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r6.claim: A reading transmitted from Nāfiʿ has one nūn, making three reading forms in all, comparable to the reading in al-Zumar.
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r6.anchor: وروي عن نافع أنه يقرأ بنون واحدة، فتكملت ثلاث قراءات

SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says waw implies the addressees already know Solomon is richer but sent aid anyway, whereas faʾ suggests they did not know and are now told he needs no aid.
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r7.anchor: إذا قلته بالواو فقد جعلت مخاطبي عالما بزيادتي عليه في الغنى

SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r8.claim: The author questions whether waw versus faʾ alone conveys that distinction and says al-Zamakhsharī also leaves unanswered why Solomon attributes wealth to God instead of saying he is richer.
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r8.anchor: وفي هذا الفرق نظر؛ إذ لا يفهم ذلك بمجرد الواو والفاء

SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r9.claim: Solomon credits God for his wealth to acknowledge the divine favor and avoid boasting.
SAMIN-DURR:27:36/r9.anchor: أنه أسند إيتاء الغنى إلى الله إظهارا لنعمته عليه

SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r1.claim: Bal antum is a transition: after rejecting the offer and explaining the rejection, Solomon shifts to the motive—their delight in worldly gain, the only cause of satisfaction they recognize.

SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī notes that the annexation of “your gift” could refer either to its giver or its recipient.
SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r2.anchor: والهدية يجوز إضافته إلى المهدي. وإلى المهدى إليه وهي هنا محتملة للأمرين

SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r3.claim: The Shaykh prefers annexation to the recipient; he also allows annexation to the giver, meaning they rejoice proudly in their gift.
SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهي هنا مضافة للمهدى إليه. وهذا هو الظاهر

SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r4.claim: The author rejects the recipient as the apparent possessor: there is no report that Solomon sent them a gift, so the annexation must refer to the giver.
SAMIN-DURR:27:36#2/r4.anchor: لم ينقل أن سليمان صلى الله عليه وسلم أرسل إليهم هدية في هذه الحالة

ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r5.claim: Although other gift accounts are reported, Solomon's question about wealth indicates the gift was money.
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r5.anchor: مما يدل على أن الهدية كانت مالا

ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r7.claim: The arrival may be the queen's messenger or her gift; the next command addresses the messenger, favoring the first reading.

ASAD-NOTES:27:36#n27/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:36#n27/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:27:36#n27/r1.claim: What God gave Solomon includes worldly wealth as well as faith, wisdom, and insight into normally hidden realities.
ASAD-NOTES:27:36#n27/r1.anchor: I.e., not only worldly wealth but also faith, wisdom and an insight into realities normally hidden from other men.

ASAD-NOTES:27:36#n28/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:36#n28/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:27:36#n28/r1.claim: Solomon characterizes them as people who prize material things alone and lack awareness of spiritual values.
ASAD-NOTES:27:36#n28/r1.anchor: I.e., people who prize only material things and have no inkling of spiritual values.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r1.claim: These readers use two nuns and retain the yāʾ in connection; another transmission from Nafi has one light nun and yāʾ in pause and connection.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو: (أتمدونني) بنونين وياء في الوصل.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r2.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r2.claim: Al-Musayyibi's transmission from Nafi reads أتمدوني with one light nun and yāʾ in both pause and connection.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r2.anchor: عن المسيبي عن نافع: (أتمدوني) خفيفة النون وهي بنون واحدة وياء في الوصل والوقف .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم والكسائي وحمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r3.claim: Ibn Amir, Asim, and al-Kisai omit yāʾ in connection and pause; Hamza has one doubled nun and pauses on yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم والكسائي: أتمدونن بغير ياء في الوصل والوقف. وقرأ حمزة: (أتمدوني بمال) بنون واحدة مشددة

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r4.claim: Abu Zayd distinguishes إمداد as supplying people with money or men; the Quran also uses مدّ for extending or increasing.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r4.anchor: أبو زيد: أمددت الرجل بالمال والرجال إمدادا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r5.claim: أتمدونني has a nominative marker nun and an object pronoun nun; the doubled reading assimilates them, while the light form drops the second nun.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r5.anchor: فالنون الأولى علامة الرفع، والثانية التي تصحب ضمير المتكلم المنصوب.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r6.claim: The yāʾ remains in connection because the phrase is not a pause; the second nun is not obligatory and may be unassimilated.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p387/r6.anchor: ألا ترى أنها تجري في الكلام ولا يلزق بها الثانية نحو: أتمدون زيدا،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p389/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p389/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p389/r1.claim: These readers omit the yāʾ in فما آتان; Abu Amr, Nafi, and Hafs read فما آتاني with fatḥa on yāʾ, and al-Kisai inclines the ت.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p389/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: (فما أتان الله) بكسر النون من غير ياء.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r1.claim: The nūns may assimilate with shadda while retaining yāʾ in pause and connection; alternatively they remain distinct, with yāʾ retained only in connection or omitted in both positions. Earlier parallels explain the forms.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r1.anchor: بإدغام النون في النون والتشديد وإثبات الياء وصلا ووقفا وبإظهار النونين

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r2.speaker: الأئمة
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r2.claim: The lengthened reading derives ātānī from giving; the author says the imams read it this way.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r2.anchor: فالحجة لمن مد أنه جعله من الإعطاء وبه قرأت الأئمة

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r3.claim: The shortened reading derives the form from coming rather than giving.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r3.anchor: والحجة لمن قصر أنه جعله من المجيء ومن أثبت الياء وفتحها

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r4.claim: The yāʾ may be retained with fatḥa or sukūn, or omitted; fatḥa avoids two adjacent sukūns, while deletion is allowed because its kasra suffices. Imāla and plain pronunciation are also reported, with earlier rationale.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p271/r4.anchor: ومن أثبت الياء وفتحها كره إسكانها فتذهب لالتقاء الساكنين والحجة لمن حذفها أنه اجتزأ بالكسرة منها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r1.claim: Abu Ja'far's reading was transmitted through Abdullah ibn Ayyash to Ubayy and the Prophet.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر على عبد الله بن عياش وقرأ عبد الله بن عياش على أبي بن كعب

IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r2.speaker: ابن أبي الزناد
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r2.claim: Ibn Abi al-Zinad says no one was more proficient in the Sunnah recitation than Abu Ja'far, who was preferred in his era over Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي الزناد قال لم يكن أحد أقرأ للسنة من أبي جعفر وكان يقدم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r3.speaker: يعقوب بن جعفر بن أبي كثير الأنصاري
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r3.claim: Abu Ja'far was the leading reader in Medina and learned from Ibn Abbas and his patron Abdullah ibn Ayyash.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r3.anchor: يعقوب بن جعفر بن أبي كثير الأنصاري قال كان إمام الناس بالمدينة أبو جعفر يزيد بن القعقاع

IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r5.claim: Abu Ja'far taught in the Prophet's mosque before the Harra, during Yazid ibn Muawiya's time, before the event in 63 AH.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r5.anchor: أخبرني أبو جعفر أنه كان يقرىء القرآن في مسجد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل الحرة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r6.claim: Abu Ja'far held the muṣḥaf for his patron Ibn Ayyash, one of the leading readers, followed his recitation, and took his reading from him.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r6.anchor: أخبرني أبو جعفر أنه كان يمسك على مولاه عبد الله بن عياش

IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r7.speaker: أم سلمة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r7.claim: Umm Salama blessed Abu Ja'far when he was brought to her as a young child.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p56/r7.anchor: أتي به إلى أم سلمة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو صغير فمسحت على رأسه ودعت له بالبركة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p96/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p96/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p96/r1.claim: Ibn Mujahid says he records variant transmissions from Asim's additional transmitters at the relevant reading locations when they differ from other transmitters.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p96/r1.anchor: وقد ذكرت ما روى غير هؤلاء عن عاصم في المواضع التي رويت عن الذي رواه وأوصله إلي

NASHR:v2p182/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p182/r8.speaker: الخمسة المذكورون أولا ومعهم حمزة
NASHR:v2p182/r8.claim: The five readers named earlier and Ḥamza retain the yāʾ in atumiddūnanī bi-māl.
NASHR:v2p182/r8.anchor: واتفق الخمسة المذكورون أولا ومعهم حمزة على إثبات الياء في أتمدونني بمال

NASHR:v2p182/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p182/r9.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v2p182/r9.claim: Ḥamza departs from his usual rule by retaining the yāʾ in both connected and paused positions, like Ibn Kathīr and Yaʿqūb.
NASHR:v2p182/r9.anchor: إلا أن حمزة خالف أصله فأثبتها في الحالين مثل ابن كثير ويعقوب

NASHR:v2p337/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p337/r9.speaker: يعقوب وحمزة
NASHR:v2p337/r9.claim: Yaʿqūb and Ḥamza assimilate the nūn in أتمدونني under the rules of major assimilation.
NASHR:v2p337/r9.anchor: وتقدم إدغام أتمدونني ليعقوب وحمزة في باب الإدغام الكبير

NASHR:v2p337/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p337/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p337/r10.claim: The author refers the readings of آتاني, آتيك, and كافرين to his earlier discussion of imāla.
NASHR:v2p337/r10.anchor: وتقدم آتان، وآتيك، وكافرين في باب الإمالة

NASHR:v2p340/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p340/r7.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو وابن كثير ويعقوب وحمزة
NASHR:v2p340/r7.claim: The Medinans and Abū ʿAmr retain the added yāʾ in connected reading; Ibn Kathīr, Yaʿqūb, and Ḥamza retain it both connected and at pause, assimilating the nūns.
NASHR:v2p340/r7.anchor: أتمدونني بمال أثبتها وصلا المدنيان، وأبو عمرو

NASHR:v2p340/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p340/r8.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو وحفص ويعقوب
NASHR:v2p340/r8.claim: The Medinans, Abū ʿAmr, and Ḥafṣ retain the opened yāʾ in connected reading; Yaʿqūb retains it at pause. Reports differ for Abū ʿAmr, Qālūn, Qunbul, and Ḥafṣ.
NASHR:v2p340/r8.anchor: آتان الله أثبتها مفتوحة وصلا المدنيان، وأبو عمرو وحفص ورويس

NASHR:v1p303/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p303/r4.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب
NASHR:v1p303/r4.claim: Ḥamza and Yaʿqūb assimilate the two nūns; the others articulate them. All codices write two nūns, and the assimilators agree on lengthening the alif and wāw before the consonant cluster.
NASHR:v1p303/r4.anchor: أتمدونني بمال في النمل أدغم النون في النون حمزة ويعقوب،

NASHR:v2p187/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p187/r5.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر وحفص ورويس
NASHR:v2p187/r5.claim: In آتان الله, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Abu Jaʿfar, Hafs, and Ruways affirm the yāʾ open in connected recitation; the excerpt then begins to list its deletion readers.
NASHR:v2p187/r5.anchor: أما آتان الله فأثبت الياء فيها مفتوحة وصلا نافع وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر وحفص ورويس

QIRAAT-ER:27:36:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:6#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:6#1/r1.claim: This canonical form keeps the full yāʾ on the first-person pronoun, extending the ending without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:6#1/r1.anchor: Canonical reading with full yāʾ on pronoun — extended first-person singular ending

QIRAAT-ER:27:36:6#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:6#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:6#2/r1.claim: At pause, the canonical variant may drop or retain the yāʾ according to dialectal pausal convention.
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:6#2/r1.anchor: Canonical variant with pause form dropping yāʾ or retaining it — dialectal pause conventions

QIRAAT-ER:27:36:6#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:6#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:6#3/r1.claim: Assimilation merges nūn al-wiqāya into the following nūn as a phonological simplification.
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:6#3/r1.anchor: Canonical variant with assimilation of nūn al-wiqāya into the following nūn

QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#1/r1.claim: This shortened pronoun form drops the final yāʾ while keeping the same meaning, as a dialectal pause form.
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant with shortened pronoun — drops final yāʾ; same meaning

QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#2/r1.claim: The canonical variants allow a full yāʾ, deleted yāʾ, or fatḥa on the yāʾ.
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#2/r1.anchor: Canonical variants with three phonological options — full yāʾ, deleted yāʾ, or fatḥa on yāʾ

QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#3/r1.claim: This pair distinguishes the pausal form ātān from the connected form ātāniya.
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#3/r1.anchor: Canonical variant pair — pause form (ātān) and connected form (ātāniya)

QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#4/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#4/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#4/r1.claim: Among the ten readings, the form has either a full yāʾ or a fatḥa-yāʾ, with no semantic difference.
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#4/r1.anchor: Ten-reading canonical — full yāʾ or fatḥa-yāʾ; no semantic difference

QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#5/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#5/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#5/r1.claim: The ten-reading variant permits either the long or short pronoun ending.
QIRAAT-ER:27:36:11#5/r1.anchor: Ten-reading canonical — long or short pronoun ending

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r10.claim: Solomon's question rejects the offer as paltry and shows his detachment from worldly wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r10.anchor: استفهام إنكار واستقلال، وفي ذلك دلالة على عزوفه عن الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r11.claim: Solomon says God's gifts of prophethood and a vast kingdom are better than the Queen's gift; their joy reflects love of worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r11.anchor: ثم ذكر نعمة الله عليه، وأن ما آتاه الله من النبوة وسعة الملك خير مما آتاكم، بل أنتم بما يهدى إليكم تفرحون بحبكم الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r12.claim: The gift is apparently ascribed to its recipient, but may instead be ascribed to its giver or stand for rejection: take it back and rejoice in it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r12.anchor: والهدية تصح إضافتها إلى المهدي وإلى المهدى إليه، وهي هنا مضافة للمهدى إليه، وهذا هو الظاهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r13.claim: On the giver-based reading, the Queen's people boast of sending a royal gift; alternatively Solomon tells them to take it back and rejoice in it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r13.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون مضافة إلى المهدي، أي بل أنتم بهديتكم هذه التي أهديتموها تفرحون فرح افتخار على الملوك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r14.speaker: جمهور السبعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r14.claim: Most of the Seven read أتمدونني with two nūns; some retain the yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r14.anchor: وقرأ جمهور السبعة: أتمدونني، بنونين، وأثبت بعض الياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r15.speaker: حمزة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r15.claim: Ḥamza assimilates the indicative nūn into the protective nūn and retains the yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r15.anchor: وقرأ حمزة: بإدغام نون الرفع في نون الوقاية وإثبات ياء المتكلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r16.speaker: المسيبي عن نافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r16.claim: Al-Musayyibī from Nāfiʿ reads one light nūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r16.anchor: وقرأ المسيبي، عن نافع: بنون واحدة خفيفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r17.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r17.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says waw assumes the envoys know Solomon is wealthier yet offer money; fa instead implies they do not know his state, so he informs them he needs no support.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r17.anchor: قال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: ما الفرق بين قولك: أتمدونني بمال وأنا أغنى منكم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: The seven emphatic consonants block imāla when adjacent before alif: both raise the tongue toward the upper palate, so the emphatic articulation prevails.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: The same emphatics generally block imāla when they follow alif or are separated from it by one or two letters.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.anchor: ناقد وعاطس وعاصم وعاضد وعاظل وناخل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: He compares the sound substitution صقت for صبقت: before qāf, speakers replace the nearer sibilant with a sound closer to qāf in articulation.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.anchor: ونحو من هذا قولهم صقت لما كان بعدها القاف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: An emphatic one letter before alif does not block imāla when that letter is preceded by kasra; lowering the tongue is easier than raising it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.anchor: فإذا كان حرف من هذه الحروف قبل الألف بحرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: With an initial kasra and two intervening letters, a silent emphatic can allow imāla because the earlier kasra makes the alif behave as if the emphatic were kasra.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.anchor: وإذا كان أول الحرف مكسورا وبين الكسرة والألف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: بعض من يقول قفاف
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: Some speakers who imale قفاف still use fatḥ in مصباح: the silent emphatic is followed by fatḥa, making it act like an emphatic followed by alif; both patterns are Arabic.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.anchor: وبعض من يقول قفاف ويميل ألف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: He records imāla in قزحا and ضمنا, and in عرقا and ملغا, by analogy with patterns such as صفاف, قفاف, غانم, and قائم.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.anchor: وتقول رأيت قزحا وأتيت ضمنا فتميل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: Alifs in ناب, مال, and باع remain subject to imāla because they stand where yā would; خاف, feminine حبلى, and غزا have comparable underlying causes.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.anchor: فأما ناب ومال وباع فإنه من

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: The alif in geminate فاعل and in مفاعل is not normally imaled: the consonant before it is open and no kasra follows it.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: Some imale مال in the genitive by analogy with مالك when the following kāf is a proper name; other speakers imale it in every case to show its original kasra.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: بعضهم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: Some speakers use fatḥ in مال قاسم, مال ملق, and مال ينقل, especially before connected emphatics; one group distinguishes a separated following word from a connected one.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.anchor: وقال بعضهم مررت بمال قاسم ومررت بمال ملق

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: Imāla persists in stable forms such as عماد and عابد before a separate قاسم because their endings do not vary by case, unlike مال.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.anchor: وقالوا هذا عماد قاسم وهذا عالم قاسم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: They do not imale in لم يضربها الذي تعلم because the alif has disappeared; it is unlike the enduring alif in حبلى or مرمى.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.anchor: فلم يميلوا لأن الألف قد ذهبت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: They open أراد أن يضبطا before emphatic ṭāʾ, but imale يعقلا because qāf is kasra; some analogically imale عرقا and ضيقا, though Sībawayh calls such forms rare.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.anchor: وقالوا أراد أن يعقلا لأن القاف مكسورة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: Particles حتى, أما, إلا, لا, and ما generally resist imāla, unlike nouns; al-Khalīl allows it if a particle is used as a personal name, and أنى is imaled as a noun-like adverb.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: Letter names با and تا are imaled as nouns for spoken letters, and يا in يا زيد is imaled because of its yā.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.anchor: ما يلفظ به وليس فيها ما في قد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.claim: Even speakers who imale مال do not generally imale hollow forms such as ساق, قار, or غاب; the medial weak alif is stronger and the imāla is less accepted.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفا.anchor: ساق ولا قار ولا غاب وغاب الأجمة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r1.claim: Rāʾ behaves as if doubled, so it prevents imāla in راشد and فراش and strengthens fatḥ of nearby alifs.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r1.anchor: والراء إذا تكلمت بها خرجت كأنها مضاعفة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r2.claim: When rāʾ follows an alif, the alif is not imaled in nominative or accusative forms like حمار; in genitive it is imaled because rāʾ acts like two kasra consonants.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r2.anchor: لم تمل في الرفع والنصب وذلك قولك هذا حمار

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r3.claim: A kasra on rāʾ after alif can overcome an earlier emphatic, allowing imāla in قارب, غارم, and طارد.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r3.anchor: ومما تغلب فيه الراء قولك قارب وغارم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r4.claim: Forms such as فارق and مفاريق take fatḥ like ناعق, منافق, and مناشيط because an emphatic follows the alif.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r4.anchor: فارق وأينق مفاريق فتنصب كما فعلت ذلك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r5.claim: Some Arabs imale الكافرون, الكافرين, الكافر, and المنابر when a consonant separates rāʾ from alif; rāʾ is distant and close in articulation to yā.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r5.anchor: واعلم أن قوما من العرب يقولون الكافرون

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r6.claim: Another group opens these alifs in nominative and accusative but imales them in genitive, treating case as the condition for imāla.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r6.anchor: في الجر كما أمالوا حيث لم يكن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r7.speaker: بعض من يقول مررت بالحمار
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r7.claim: Some who say مررت بالحمار still pronounce مررت بالكافر with fatḥ, since their usual form عابد has an open alif and the ending varies.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r7.anchor: مررت بالكافر فينصب الألف وذلك لأنك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r8.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r8.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r8.claim: Imāla in كافر is more common than in قادر because qāf is emphatic; some Arabs with sound Arabic nevertheless imale قادر when rāʾ is kasra.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r8.anchor: واعلم أن من يقول مررت بكافر أكثر ممن يقول

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r9.speaker: هدبة بن خشرم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r9.claim: Hudbah ibn Khashram's verse uses قادر with imāla, witnessing the reported variant مررت بقادر before kasra on rāʾ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r9.anchor: لهدبة بن خشرم # % عسى الله يغني عن بلاد ابن قادر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r10.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r10.claim: They often open حمار قاسم for qāf, though imāla is more common than in مال قاسم because the intervening pattern has two kasras; جارم قاسم does not behave identically.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r10.anchor: فينصبون للقاف كما نصبوا حين قالوا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r11.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r11.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r11.claim: Speakers who say حمار قاسم also say سفار قبل because rāʾ can change in construct phrases or as the ending of a masculine name.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r11.anchor: قال مررت بسفار قبل لأن الراء هاهنا يدركها التغيير

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r12.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r12.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r12.claim: In فار قبل and كافر قبل, a single silent consonant intervenes and the following rāʾ is kasra, making imāla required for these speakers; a speaker who says جاد does not say فار.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r12.anchor: وتقول مررت بفار قبل في لغة من قال

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r14.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r14.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r14.claim: Imāla in دنانير is more expected because rāʾ is farther from the alif; genitive behavior matches كافر, and some speakers also say مناشيط.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r14.anchor: وتقول هذه دنانير كما قلت كافر فهذا أجدر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r15.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r15.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r15.claim: At pause, forms such as داع do not imale because the kasra is not pronounced; in حمار, the doubled rāʾ similarly governs the preceding alif.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r15.anchor: واعلم أن الذين يقولون هذا داع في السكوت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r16.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r16.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r16.claim: Some imale the hāʾ and preceding vowel in مهارى; Arab forms ضربة and أخذه liken hāʾ to alif, so the preceding sound is imaled.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r16.anchor: تميل الهاء وما قبلها وقال سمعت العرب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r17.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r17.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r17.claim: The rāʾ is weaker than qāf in these contexts: speakers who say أراد أن يضربها قاسم also say راشد, and those who say بمال قاسم also say بمال راشد.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r17.anchor: قاسم قال أراد أن يضربها راشد ومن قال بمال

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r18.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r18.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r18.claim: Forms عفرا, عيرا, and عمران can be compared with علقا, ضيقا, and حمقان; some imale عفرا because initial kasra precedes a final alif, treating it like حبلى.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r18.anchor: فيميلون للكسرة لأن الألف في آخر الحرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r19.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r19.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r19.claim: Imāla in عفرا is especially plausible by analogy with عرقا and forms of يعقرها; if kasra can incline the alif, yā is an even stronger trigger.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r19.anchor: وكان هذا ألزم حيث قال بعضهم رأيت عرقا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r20.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r20.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r20.claim: They imale النغران because initial kasra precedes an alif after a root consonant, which they liken to an alif built into a word such as حبلى.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r20.anchor: النغران حيث كسرت أول الحرف وكانت الألف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r21.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r21.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r21.claim: They say عمران with imāla but not برقان or حمقان because those forms contain emphatic consonants.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r22.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r22.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r22.claim: Some who imale عمران also imale عقران, since the emphatic is distant; in فراش and جراب fatḥ is preferred because their alif is added, not like feminine حبلى.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r22.anchor: في رجل يسمى عقران هذا عقران

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r1.claim: A subjunctive after أو is governed by an understood أن, as after fa and wāw; أن is not normally stated aloud.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r1.anchor: اعلم أن ما انتصب بعد أو فإنه ينتصب على إضمار أن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r2.claim: The subjunctive after أو can mean إلا أن; Imruʾ al-Qays's أو نموت فنعذرا means unless we die, parallel to لألزمنك أو تقضيني.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r3.claim: Rafʿ after أو is grammatical either by coordinating the following clause with the first or by starting a new clause.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r3.anchor: ولو رفعت لكان عربيا جائزا على وجهين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r5.speaker: ذوا الرمة
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r5.claim: Dhū al-Rumma's verse allows either coordination with لا تنفك or a new clause at أو نرمي بها.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r6.claim: In commands such as الزمه أو يتقيك, the subjunctive means unless he protects you; raising is a fresh clause because the clauses cannot be coordinated.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r7.speaker: زياد الأعجم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r7.claim: Ziyād al-Aʿjam's verse وكنت إذا غمزت قناة قوم كسرت كعوبها أو تستقيما illustrates subjunctive with the sense إلا أن; rafʿ would instead start a clause.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r7.anchor: وقال زياد الأعجم # % وكنت إذا غمزت قناة قوم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r8.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r8.speaker: طرفة بن العبد
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r8.claim: Ṭarafa's أو أنا مفتدي exemplifies a raised independent clause after هو قاتلي أو أفتدي منه.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r10.speaker: الحصين بن حمام المري
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r10.claim: The poem ولولا رجال ... أو أسوءك shows an understood أن because the verb cannot be coordinated directly with لولا.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r13.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r13.speaker: عمرو بن معدي كرب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r13.claim: The line تحية بينهم ضرب وجيع supports the idiom comparing a state or greeting with an action, which Sībawayh uses to explain the Medinan reading.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r13.anchor: وقال الشاعر وهو عمرو ابن معدي كرب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r14.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r14.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r14.claim: For the Aʿshā's إن تركبوا ... أو تنزلون, al-Khalīl parses the clauses as alternatives: one would be the case or the other, as if أتركبون were used.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r15.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r15.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r15.claim: Yūnus raises أو تنزلون as a fresh clause, understood as أو أنتم نازلون; Sībawayh says this analysis is easier and applies it to أو يرسل in the verse.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r17.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r17.speaker: زهير
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r17.claim: Al-Khalīl compares the strained coordination analysis with Zuhayr's ولا سابق شيئا إذا كان جائيا, where coordination is only imagined from the sense.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r17.anchor: وأما الخليل فجعله بمنزلة قول زهير

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r18.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r18.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r18.claim: Sībawayh says the coordination analysis is remote because if it were ordinary coordination it would also work after fa and wāw; the semantic relation can instead prompt a new clause, as in لا تأته فيشتمك.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r18.anchor: والإشراك على هذا التوهم بعيد كبعد ولا سابق شيئا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r1.claim: The wording omits the sending of the gift: she sent it, and when it reached Solomon, he spoke. The alternative takes the subject of “came” as the queen sending it; the first is preferable.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r1.anchor: في الكلام حذف أي فارسلت الهدية فلما جاء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r2.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads the verb in the plural, “when they came,” referring to the messengers.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r2.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ( فلما جاؤا ) أي المرسلون

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r3.claim: The address may be to the envoy while grammatically including the sender, or to the envoy and his party; al-Ālūsī prefers the former because it extends the rebuke to the queen and her people, in keeping with the singular return command.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r3.anchor: خطاب للرسول والمرسل تغليبا للحاضر على الغائب

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r4.claim: The indefinite form of māl belittles the wealth offered.

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r5.speaker: جمهور السبعة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r5.claim: Most of the seven readers pronounce two nūns in tamuddūnani; some also retain the speaker's yāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r5.anchor: قرأ جمهور السبعة ( تمدونن ) بنونين وأثبت بعض الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r6.speaker: حمزة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r6.claim: Ḥamza assimilates the indicative nūn into the protective nūn and retains the first-person yāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r6.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بادغام نون الرفع في نون الوقاية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r7.speaker: المسيبي عن نافع
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r7.claim: Al-Musayyibī from Nāfiʿ reads a single light nūn, with the protective nūn omitted; an alternative analysis omits the first nūn and assumes an unexpressed inflectional marker.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r7.anchor: وقرأ المسيبي عن نافع بنون واحدة خفيفة والمحذوف نون الوقاية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r8.claim: What God gave Solomon is primarily prophethood and unexcelled sovereignty, compared with their wealth; taking it as material wealth is possible but less eloquent and less fitting.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r8.anchor: أي من النبوة والملك الذي لاغاية وراءه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r9.claim: The sentence explains the rejection indirectly: Solomon needs no gift and assigns it no value, rather than boasting about what he received.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r9.anchor: والكلام كناية عن عدم القبول لهديتهم وليس المراد منه الافتخار

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r10.claim: The apparent sequence has Solomon say this as soon as the envoys arrive, perhaps from eagerness to guide them; another view places it after the exchanges reported by Wahb and others.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r10.anchor: والظاهر أن الخطاب المذكور كان أول ما جاؤه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r11.claim: The verse supports recommending the return of gifts from polytheists when doing so serves a religious interest, not as an unconditional rule.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r11.anchor: واستدل بالآية على استحباب رد هدايا المشركين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r12.claim: He did not phrase the clause as “what God gave me is better than what He gave you” so it could serve as a circumstantial clause: a confirmatory state must be known, whereas this reason was not.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200/r12.anchor: وإنما لم يقل : وما آتاني الله خير مما آتاكم لتكون الجملة حالا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r1.claim: One reading takes the clause as a shift from rejecting the gift to exposing the envoys' worldly outlook: they rejoice in gifts because their aspirations are confined to worldly increase.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r1.anchor: إلى بيان ما حملهم عليه من قياس حاله عليه السلام على حالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r2.claim: Another reading reproaches them for rejoicing in their gift to Solomon with pride, a sense of obligation, or self-regard; this makes their presumption in treating him as a great king especially blameworthy.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r2.anchor: إلى التوبيخ بفرحهم بهديتهم التي أهدوها إليه عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r3.claim: The possessive construction can attribute the gift either to its recipient or to its giver.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r3.anchor: والهدية مضافة إلى المهدى إليه وهي تضاف إلى ذلك كما تضاف إلى المهدى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r4.claim: They may rejoice because they expect a greater return, material or otherwise, from a gift to a ruler, such as preventing their lands from being destroyed.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r4.anchor: من حيث توقعهم به ما هو أزيد منه فان الهدايا للعظماء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r5.claim: A subtler view makes this a euphemistic refusal: they should take back the gift and rejoice in receiving it, since Solomon has no need of it; al-Ālūsī calls this reading obscure.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r5.anchor: أنتم من حقكم تفرحوا بأخذ الهدية لا أنا فخذوها وافرحوا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p200#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
